thread:
Maya Chen: quick question — migrating analytics s3-uploader SA to the new terraform module. after apply pods get AWS 403 when calling S3. TF sets an annotation on the SA: iam.amazonaws.com/role: arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/rdw-analytics-s3-uploader. is that the right annotation for IRSA?
Tom Reynolds: nope — IRSA expects the annotation key to be `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`. you can paste the rendered SA yaml?
Maya Chen: here is the TF snippet we used:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "s3_uploader" {
  metadata {
    name = "s3-uploader"
    namespace = "analytics"
    annotations = {
      "iam.amazonaws.com/role" = "arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/rdw-analytics-s3-uploader"
    }
  }
}
```
Jin Park: yep that's the issue. change to `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` and reapply. also confirm the OIDC provider is created for the cluster — IRSA won't work without it.
Priya Singh: quick RBAC check: make sure the SA is bound to a Role/ClusterRole that allows access to any k8s secrets or resources the uploader needs. example Role + RoleBinding (namespace-scoped):
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: s3-uploader-writer
  namespace: analytics
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: bind-s3-uploader
  namespace: analytics
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: s3-uploader
  namespace: analytics
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: s3-uploader-writer
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
Maya Chen: interesting — we had a ClusterRoleBinding in the old setup. TF module created a namespaced RoleBinding against a ClusterRole name `s3-writer`. could that be a cause?
Tom Reynolds: that should be fine for k8s RBAC as long as the role has the right verbs. but the 403 from AWS is separate — that's the IAM side (IRSA). logs from the app show: `failed to get credentials: AccessDenied` and the AWS STS assume-role call is failing.
infra-bot: quick tip — confirm the SA yaml on cluster: `kubectl get sa s3-uploader -n analytics -o yaml` and check `.metadata.annotations`. Also run `aws iam get-role --role-name rdw-analytics-s3-uploader` to validate the role exists and its trust policy includes the OIDC provider with `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` for the proper `sub` condition.
Maya Chen: ran the get, it has the wrong annotation key indeed. changing now to:
```hcl
annotations = {
  "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = "arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/rdw-analytics-s3-uploader"
}
```
Maya Chen: also noticed our TF module had `automount_service_account_token = false` by default, I flipped it to true (we rely on projected tokens).
Jin Park: good call — projected tokens are required for IRSA to present the web identity token to AWS. if it's false the SDK won't have credentials.
Priya Singh: couple more checks: 1) the IAM role trust policy should include `StringEquals` for `sts:aud` and the `sub` like `system:serviceaccount:analytics:s3-uploader`. 2) if you use a custom audience, ensure the pod uses the projected token with that audience.
Maya Chen: changed annotation + enabled automount, re-deployed pods. first pod logs now show successful S3 ListBucket. :tada:
Tom Reynolds: awesome. thanks for the quick patch — can we add a unit test in the TF module that asserts the annotation key and automount are set? small PR would prevent regressions.
Maya Chen: on it, will open PR today. cc @deploy-bot to trigger a canary redeploy after merge.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for analytics namespace in 10m :rocket:
Maya Chen: thanks y'all — saved my morning. :pray:
